title: Trump Group Sells an Estates at Acqualina Penthouse for $33M - the Tower's Priciest Sale Yet
summary: An affiliate of Jules and Eddie Trump's Trump Group sold the 52nd-floor unit at the Estates at Acqualina, 17975 Collins Avenue in Sunny Isles Beach, for $33 million - the highest price recorded in the tower to date. Buyer Acquilina 26 LLC, tied to consultant Lindsay Levert and Hallandale Beach real estate attorney Maria Marta Calderon, financed with a $20.5 million Morgan Stanley loan. The roughly 8,858-square-foot, six-bedroom, 7.5-bath unit sold furnished after asking $35 million, penciling to roughly $3,725 per square foot. The two oceanfront towers, completed in 2022 and 2023, hold 232 units combined; earlier this year a 7,700-square-foot Estates condo traded at $21.6 million, or about $2,800 per foot. The Trump Group is unrelated to President Donald Trump.

title: Phoenix Realty Pays $64.8M for 269-Unit Bay Pointe in South Miami-Dade at ~$240,900 Per Door
summary: New York-based Phoenix Realty Group bought the 269-unit Bay Pointe Apartments at 18422 Homestead Avenue in unincorporated south Miami-Dade from an entity tied to Pride Homes by Garco for $64.8 million - about $240,892 per unit - assuming the seller's $55.2 million Corebridge Institutional Investments loan. The seven-story building was completed in 2024 on 2.4 acres with 134 one-bedroom, 129 two-bedroom and six three-bedroom apartments plus 3,700 square feet of retail. The trade extends a recovering cycle: South Florida multifamily sales totaled $2.5 billion in the first half, up 19.4 percent year over year per Avison Young, and 12-month leasing of 13,774 units finally edged past the 12,751 units delivered per CoStar. Nearly 28,000 units remain under construction, many due late next year.

title: Baptist Health Buys a Coconut Creek Kohl's for $53.5M - $577 Per Foot on 8.2 Acres
summary: Baptist Health South Florida paid $53.5 million for the stand-alone Kohl's at 6950 North State Road 7 in Coconut Creek, or $577 per square foot for a 92,700-square-foot store on 8.2 acres that Kohl's bought for $14.8 million in 2008. The store remains open while Baptist evaluates plans for the site. Baptist is the region's largest hospital operator, with 12 hospitals and roughly 200 care and office facilities, and is also building a 61,000-square-foot Pembroke Pines medical center opening early next year and the 340,000-square-foot Baptist Health Sunrise Hospital due in 2029. Large medical anchors tend to lift surrounding retail, office and residential values, which is why big-box parcels near health-system expansion keep clearing well above traditional retail pricing.

title: Mortgage Rates Climb to 6.71%; 15-Year Back Above 6% and Jumbo Averages Near 6.8%
summary: Freddie Mac's Primary Mortgage Market Survey put the 30-year fixed at 6.71 percent for the week ended September 3, up from 6.66 percent the prior week and above the 6.50 percent averaged a year ago. The 15-year fixed averaged 6.04 percent, up from 5.98 percent and back over 6 percent. Daily jumbo averages moved with it, running near 6.78 percent in the days after the print. For South Florida buyers and investors the practical read is that financing costs are grinding sideways-to-higher rather than easing, which keeps pressure on debt-service coverage for new acquisitions and continues to favor assumable-loan and seller-financed structures.

title: Palm Beach's Landmark 'Ham and Cheese House' Lists at $105M - Nearly $8,000 Per Foot
summary: Casa Eleda at 920 South Ocean Boulevard - the Maurice Fatio-designed brick-and-coquina landmark nicknamed the 'Ham and Cheese House' for its red-and-white facade - hit the market at $105 million, about $7,972 per square foot across 13,200 square feet on roughly an acre. Built for early-1900s banker Mortimer Schiff and named for his wife Adele ('Eleda' backward), it last sold for nearly $16 million in 2013 to the late industrialist Marion Antonini and his wife Penelope, so the ask is more than six times the 2013 basis. Seven bedrooms, 10 full and four half baths, wine cellar, and a tunnel running to a beachfront cabana; Christian Angle of Christian Angle Real Estate has the listing, first reported by the Wall Street Journal. In the same Palm Beach County roundup: Freedom Mortgage CEO Stanley Middleman listed his Ocean Ridge oceanfront estate at 6161 North Ocean Boulevard for $60 million ($5,699 per foot), and a Boca Raton yacht-club home traded at $20 million.

title: Manalapan Lake-to-Ocean Homesite Trades at $30M After More Than Quadrupling in 11 Years
summary: A company managed by auto dealer Ralph Gesualdo sold the nearly 2-acre lake-to-ocean parcel at 1820 South Ocean Boulevard in Manalapan for $30 million in an off-market deal to an entity tied to Palm Beach attorney Maura Ziska of Kochman & Ziska; the end buyer is undisclosed. MGM Designs paid $7 million for the site in 2015, so the price is more than four times the 2015 basis and well above this year's $19.1 million county appraiser value. The last ask was $35 million, per seller's agent Jack Elkins of William Raveis, who calls the barrier island south of Palm Beach the 'next billionaire's bunker.' The low-density residential site runs Intracoastal-to-Atlantic across Ocean Boulevard, with a 1969 cabana and a 1988 dock. Nearby comps: 1800 South Ocean at $25 million last year, Gesualdo's 1920 South Ocean to WeatherTech founder David MacNeil at $36 million in July, and Sean Hannity's 1840 South Ocean at $23.5 million two years ago; Larry Ellison also owns on the island.

title: Shoma Lands $172.5M C-PACE Construction Loan for a 333-Unit North Bay Village Condo Tower
summary: Shoma Group closed a $172.5 million construction loan from Nuveen Green Capital for Shoma Bay, the 24-story, 333-unit condo-and-retail tower at 1850 John F. Kennedy Causeway in North Bay Village; Newmark's Anthony Orso, Clifford Welden and Daniel Matz arranged the debt. Nuveen calls it one of the five largest C-PACE-financed projects in Florida - a useful marker of how far Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy debt has moved into mainstream South Florida condo capital stacks. The Coral Gables developer, led by Masoud and Stephanie Shojaee, paid about $16 million for the waterfront site in 2022 planning a rental tower, then converted to condos; a 36,000-square-foot Publix anchors the retail. Asking prices start in the $800,000s with Craig Studnicky's ISG World on sales, and the financing retires a $29.9 million Forman Capital predevelopment loan.

title: Miami Advances Little Havana and Miami River Upzoning - 150 Units Per Acre, No Affordable Mandate
summary: Miami is moving a pair of zoning and land-use changes covering 661 lots on 136 acres across 11 Little Havana and Miami River-area thoroughfares, plus a companion comprehensive-plan item retargeting 349 properties on 72 acres (47 to medium-density multifamily, 302 to restricted commercial). The changes would open T6-8 zoning - generally up to eight stories - on lots now in lower-rise districts and lift density to 150 units per acre where the baseline runs 36 to 65, potentially adding close to 20,000 residents. Despite planners citing mixed-income housing as the rationale, the proposals carry no affordable-housing guarantee, per Coconut Grove Spotlight. The Planning, Zoning and Appeals Board votes Wednesday evening and forwards a recommendation to the full city commission. Investor read: the area's single-family homes, duplexes, small apartment buildings and retail plazas reprice as land if the density lift survives to the commission.

title: Fort Lauderdale's $51M Ember House Goes Under Contract - A Record for Broward Spec Homes
summary: Dov Stark's newly built 15,000-square-foot waterfront estate at 513 Middle River Drive in Fort Lauderdale's Sunrise Intracoastal neighborhood is under contract for $51 million, per a Wall Street Journal report. The spec home listed in April at $55 million, then the priciest residential listing in Broward County. Stark, founder and CEO of Prestige Homes Development, designed, developed and listed the property and is the seller; the unidentified buyers are represented by Joelle Oiknine of One Sotheby's International Realty. The deal is set to close in January and would rank among the priciest home sales in the city. Oiknine said the buyers passed on Miami Beach and Golden Beach product before committing in Fort Lauderdale.

title: Terra Lands $245M Refi on 578-Unit Sweetwater Rental as Miami's Multifamily Oversupply Balances Out
summary: David Martin's Terra secured a $245 million permanent loan on the first phase of Upland Park, a 578-unit garden-style complex it completed this summer on a 47-acre site at 1455 Northwest 121st Avenue in Sweetwater, next to Miami-Dade's Dolphin Station Park & Ride. New York-based Slate Property Group provided the financing, retiring the $170 million construction loan Terra took from Slate affiliate Scale Lending in 2024. The refi pencils to roughly $423,875 per unit on a $1 billion completed phase, and Terra leases the land from Miami-Dade County. The deal lands as the region's rental oversupply starts to clear, a constructive signal for transit-adjacent garden-style multifamily basis.

title: Related Ross Pays $28.3M for 31-Acre Wellington Site for the K-Park Mixed-Use District
summary: Billionaire Steve Ross' Related Ross paid $28.3 million for the Village Landing site in Wellington, a 31-acre parcel at 10400 Stribling Way and State Road 7 bought from the Acme Improvement District. The purchase was backed by a $29.1 million mortgage from an entity tied to Barry Sternlicht's Starwood Capital. The land carries commercial zoning with an agricultural classification. Related Ross plans K-Park, a walkable downtown restaurant and retail district with a 180-key hotel and more than 300,000 square feet of retail, plus a private school on a separate adjacent property - continuing the firm's westward Palm Beach County land accumulation.

title: Two Roads Settles With Biscayne 21 Holdouts, Clearing a Landmark Condo-Termination Fight in Edgewater
summary: Two Roads Development, led by Taylor Collins and Reid Boren, settled with the holdout owners at Biscayne 21 in Miami's Edgewater, ending a legal fight that began in 2023 over the buyout and termination of the waterfront condo association. The owners had argued the developer-controlled association acted illegally in lowering the termination threshold from 100 percent of owners to 80 percent. Two Roads paid the holdouts for their units at an undisclosed combined price. The settlement removes a closely watched obstacle to bulk condo-termination redevelopment plays across South Florida's aging waterfront inventory.

title: Palm Beach Office-Retail Building Resells for $18M at $2,780 PSF - Double Its Price a Year Ago
summary: Delray Beach-based Redfearn Capital is selling the 6,500-square-foot Mediterranean Revival office and retail building at 317 Peruvian Avenue for $18 million, about $2,780 per square foot and more than double the $8.4 million an entity tied to Alex Redfearn paid last year. Redfearn had expected a long-term hold but said the unnamed buyer made an offer the sellers could not refuse. The 2002 building has rare on-island built-in parking and counts Sotheby's International Realty, Pizza Al Fresco and Caroline Rafferty as tenants; the county appraiser values it at $6.9 million, and it last traded in 1999 for $750,000. On-island office remains scarce - Ken Griffin sold his 50,000-square-foot Worth Avenue building for $86 million earlier this year after a three-year hold.

title: South Florida's $1B Convention Center Hotel Boom Advances on Three Fronts
summary: Related Ross' 18-story, 400-key Hilton Curio at 900 South Rosemary Avenue in West Palm Beach goes to a second city commission hearing this week. Its $290 million cost is privately financed and hinges on a $26 million sale-leaseback with Palm Beach County that takes the 1.8-acre site off the tax roll but guarantees the county $1 billion in rent over a lease of up to 99 years. In Miami Beach, Terra and Turnberry's 800-key Grand Hyatt beside the convention center topped off in July on a $392 million Tyko Capital construction loan plus $75 million in county grant funding, with completion due late next year. Broward's 801-room Omni Fort Lauderdale opened last December as part of a $1 billion-plus convention center expansion backed by $389.5 million in revenue bonds and $280 million from the county general fund.

title: Nelson Peltz Adds a $30M Mortgage on Palm Beach's Montsorrel - $98.5M Borrowed in 13 Months
summary: Trian Fund Management founder Nelson Peltz and Claudia Heffner Peltz recorded a $30 million, 15-year Bank of America mortgage on their 13-acre Palm Beach estate at 542 and 548 North County Road, about a year after a $68.5 million loan on the same property and following a $40 million loan in 2022. The county property appraiser values Montsorrel at $307 million; the Peltzes assembled the two parcels for $16.5 million in 1987 and 1988. The pattern is a reminder that ultra-high-net-worth owners are increasingly pulling liquidity out of trophy Palm Beach real estate through debt rather than selling into the island's record pricing.

title: Palm Beach County Advances a One-Year Hyperscale Data Center Moratorium; Martin County Follows
summary: County commissioners voted unanimously to pursue a full-year pause on data centers with a monthly peak load of 50 megawatts or more, matching the statewide definition adopted this year, with a final vote set for Sept. 24. New proposals have been halted since July 9, and the county rejected the 3.7 million-square-foot Project Tango data center and warehouse near Loxahatchee, a decision owner PBA Holdings is appealing. Martin County advanced its own moratorium the same week, joining Clay, Hernando and Lake counties. For owners of large west-county industrial land the practical effect is that the highest-bidding buyer pool is off the table for at least a year.
